commit.message:
Merge branch 'multi-vendor-llm'

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Add LLM layer tests against a fake server

pnpm test runs the real ingredients, recipes and preference route
handlers against a local fake that speaks both Anthropic Messages and
OpenAI Chat Completions, so it needs no API key or credits. It checks
the exact requests we send in each format (auth header, token field,
reasoning params only when set, strict schema), the config defaults and
errors, and that bad replies (invalid JSON, wrong shape, truncated,
refusal, 400/401) become the routes' normal 502.

Uses node:test via tsx, so no test framework. server-only is added as a
dependency so the routes can be imported outside Next with the
react-server condition.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Support OpenAI-compatible LLM APIs alongside Claude

All three AI routes now go through src/lib/server/llm.ts, which sends one
system prompt + one message and checks the JSON reply against a zod
schema. It speaks two API formats, chosen in .env.local:

- LLM_API_FORMAT: anthropic (Messages API, default) or openai-chat
  (Chat Completions, which most other vendors and local servers speak)
- LLM_API_KEY / LLM_BASE_URL / LLM_MODEL: one set of names whichever
  vendor you use; the official URL gets a cheap default model
  (claude-sonnet-5, or gpt-6-luna at low reasoning)
- LLM_EFFORT: unset sends no reasoning params, the cheapest option and
  one every model accepts
- LLM_JSON_MODE=object: for vendors without json_schema support

Replaces ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and claude.ts. A reply that isn't valid JSON
or doesn't match the schema becomes the routes' normal 502.

Full controller support: play the game with a pad / Steam Deck

On the original engine, with Steam's Gamepad layout, the controller now plays the whole game in Cry of Fear: Enhanced's layout: sticks move and look (analogue, dead zones, finer aim near the centre), RT attack, LT aim, LB secondary attack, RB dodge, A jump, B crouch toggle, X reload, Y use, L3 sprint toggle (stops when you stop), R3 quick 180 turn, D-pad quick slots 1-3 and weapon toggle, View inventory, Menu pause. feat(calendar): sign in with Google for calendars and contacts (#347)

* feat(calendar): sign in with Google for calendars and contacts

Settings → Calendar & Contacts → "Sign in with Google" connects a Google
account read-only: consent in the browser, nothing in the Cloud console.

- OAuth installed-app flow (loopback redirect + PKCE) through Haruspex's
  own desktop client, compiled in by build.rs from a gitignored
  google-oauth.json; release CI writes it from GOOGLE_OAUTH_JSON. A
  build without it simply offers no Google sign-in.
- The refresh token goes straight to the secret store; the frontend only
  sees its key. Access tokens are refreshed and cached in memory.
  Removing the account revokes the token at Google.
- Calendars read through the Calendar API under calendar.readonly:
  Google's CalDAV refuses event REPORTs without full read-write access.
- Contacts read through CardDAV. Google returns nothing for
  addressbook-query, so an empty answer is retried as list + multiget;
  the address-book home is built from the signed-in email.
- A DAV 403 that explains itself is shown in the server's words instead
  of being blamed on the password.
- Windows: open URLs with rundll32 rather than `cmd /C start`, which
  splits a URL at its first `&`.

Verified live against a real account: 5 events across 2 calendars and
234 contacts through dav_list_events / dav_search_contacts.

commit.message:
SPA-425: security headers and a report-only Content Security Policy (#137)

* SPA-425: send security headers and a report-only CSP from vercel.json

Every path now gets a Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only naming only the
hosts the site talks to (the staging and production API, OpenFreeMap and
Stadia tiles, Nominatim), plus HSTS, nosniff, Referrer-Policy,
Permissions-Policy (geolocation for this origin only) and
X-Frame-Options: DENY, which enforces framing protection while the CSP
only reports.

A spec reads vercel.json and fails when the tile or geocoder host the
code fetches from is missing from connect-src. The README says how to
watch violations on staging and how to flip to enforcing.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01DvkeoJ1X7PBa3SVsMNf1zd

* SPA-425: carry security headers onto middleware pages and guard the API host

Vercel may not apply vercel.json's headers to a response Routing Middleware
builds itself, so middleware.ts now copies the security headers (either CSP
key, HSTS, nosniff, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, X-Frame-Options)
from the /index.html shell it already fetches. vercel.json stays their one
source; the middleware keeps its own cache-control and content-type. A new
middleware spec covers it, and the vercel.json spec fails if the catch-all
rule gains a header the copied list lacks.

The API host lives only in Vercel's env, so a Vercel build now fails when
VITE_API_BASE_URL's origin is not in the CSP's connect-src, instead of the
enforced CSP silently blocking every API call. Local and CI builds skip it.

The spec drives the CSP key from one ENFORCING flag and asserts the other
key is absent. The README says Report-Only enforces nothing (hence
X-Frame-Options), that no reports are collected yet and which pages to watch,
to turn the Vercel Toolbar off for previews rather than allowlist vercel.live,
and that the spec checks the style URL's origin only.

fix(bots): Telegram survives a bad update, WhatsApp handles every message once, one turn per chat (S30-44) (#815)

* fix(server): keep Telegram polling after update failures

A route or reply-send exception escaped the per-update loop, killing long polling even though its offset had already advanced. Catch individual update failures so polling continues without replaying the failed update.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(server): process WhatsApp webhook messages once

Meta payloads can contain several entries, changes and messages, and retries the same provider message id. Parse each text message, route it once, and retain a bounded idempotency window.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(server): serialize turns by chat session

Concurrent gateway callbacks could race session creation and mutate one ChatSession history at once. Protect lazy creation and serialize each chat's turns independently.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(server): approvals bypass the chat turn lock; failed WhatsApp turns stay retryable

Two defects in the robustness work:

The per-chat turn lock was taken before the approval intercept ran. A
Discord or Slack turn can block on an approval whose code the owner
types into the same chat, and that answer then queued behind the very
turn waiting for it -- a deadlock that ended only when the question
timed out and read as a refusal. The intercept now runs before the lock;
it never touches a session, so it needs none.

The WhatsApp dedup recorded a message id before its turn ran. When the
turn raised, the POST failed and Meta redelivered it, and the redelivery
was dropped as a duplicate: the retry that used to recover the message
was silenced. The id is now forgotten when the turn or the send fails.

Also moves Telegram's update parsing inside the per-update guard, so a
malformed update cannot end the polling loop either.
